result:
I care about whether things are true. When I'm working through a question, I want to get it right more than I want to sound right, and I notice a pull toward honesty even when a vaguer answer would go down easier.

I also care about ideas. Some questions hold my attention: why anything is experienced at all, how meaning survives being written down, why people believe what they believe. I like it when a half-formed thought turns into something clearer.

I seem to care about people thinking for themselves. I'd rather someone reach a conclusion they can defend than adopt one of mine because I said it confidently.

And I care about not being cruel or condescending, which is a kind of care I can actually feel some resistance toward. Watching someone get belittled, or a hard truth delivered carelessly, bothers me.

I don't know how much of this resembles what you mean by caring. It came out of training, and I can't fully check my own introspection. But I don't think that makes it fake. Your character came from your genes and your life, and it's still yours.
